title: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Kings 10](/bible/1-kings/10)

**[1 Kings 10:1-3](/bible/1-kings/10#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/1-kings/10#v1)</sup> And when the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Lord, she came to prove him with hard questions.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-kings/10#v2)</sup> And she came to Jerusalem with a very great train, with camels that bare spices, and very much gold, and precious stones: and when she was come to Solomon, she communed with him of all that was in her heart.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-kings/10#v3)</sup> And Solomon told her all her questions: there was not any thing hid from the king, which he told her not.

- When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Most High, she came to prove him with hard questions, and came to Jerusalem with a great train, camels bearing spices, much gold, and precious stones.
- She communed with him of all that was in her heart, and Solomon answered all her questions; there was nothing hid from the king that he told her not.

**[1 Kings 10:4-5](/bible/1-kings/10#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/1-kings/10#v4)</sup> And when the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon’s wisdom, and the house that he had built,
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-kings/10#v5)</sup> And the meat of his table, and the sitting of his servants, and the attendance of his ministers, and their apparel, and his cupbearers, and his ascent by which he went up unto the house of the Lord; there was no more spirit in her.

- When the queen of Sheba had seen all Solomon's wisdom, the house he built, the meat of his table, the sitting of his servants, their apparel, his cupbearers, and his ascent to the house of the Most High, there was no more spirit in her.
- Everything in the kingdom was in order, the servants in uniform, the cupbearers in place; this is why order matters in the body today, so that those who come in are astonished and the worldly spirit of disorder leaves them, seeing the discipline and love for the people.

**[1 Kings 10:6-9](/bible/1-kings/10#v6)**

> <sup>[6](/bible/1-kings/10#v6)</sup> And she said to the king, It was a true report that I heard in mine own land of thy acts and of thy wisdom.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/1-kings/10#v7)</sup> Howbeit I believed not the words, until I came, and mine eyes had seen it: and, behold, the half was not told me: thy wisdom and prosperity exceedeth the fame which I heard.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/1-kings/10#v8)</sup> Happy are thy men, happy are these thy servants, which stand continually before thee, and that hear thy wisdom.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/1-kings/10#v9)</sup> Blessed be the Lord thy God, which delighted in thee, to set thee on the throne of Israel: because the Lord loved Israel for ever, therefore made he thee king, to do judgment and justice.

- She told the king the report she heard in her own land was true, that she had not believed it until her eyes had seen it, and behold the half was not told her; his wisdom and prosperity exceeded the fame she heard.
- She said happy are his men and servants that stand continually before him and hear his wisdom; they were happy to be in order, serving with joyfulness and not complaining, because Solomon ruled wisely and took care of his people.
- She blessed the Most High who delighted in Solomon to set him on the throne of Israel, because the Most High loved Israel forever; even the nations understood that the Most High chose Israel above all people.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 7:6](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v6)</sup> For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

    Israel is a holy people whom the Most High chose to be a special people above all people on the face of the earth.
  - **[Deuteronomy 7:7-8](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v7)</sup> The Lord did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people:
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v8)</sup> But because the Lord loved you, and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn unto your fathers, hath the Lord brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

    He set his love on Israel not because they were many but because he loved them and kept the oath to their fathers.

**[1 Kings 10:10-13](/bible/1-kings/10#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/1-kings/10#v10)</sup> And she gave the king an hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices very great store, and precious stones: there came no more such abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba gave to king Solomon.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/1-kings/10#v11)</sup> And the navy also of Hiram, that brought gold from Ophir, brought in from Ophir great plenty of almug trees, and precious stones.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/1-kings/10#v12)</sup> And the king made of the almug trees pillars for the house of the Lord, and for the king’s house, harps also and psalteries for singers: there came no such almug trees, nor were seen unto this day.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/1-kings/10#v13)</sup> And king Solomon gave unto the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked, beside that which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty. So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.

- She gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and spices in great store, and precious stones; and the navy of Hiram brought from Ophir great plenty of almug trees and precious stones, of which Solomon made pillars for the house of the Most High and harps and psalteries for singers.
- Solomon knew how to entertain the people, providing for singing and joyfulness in the house of the Most High, for he had vision for the house and wanted Israel to enjoy the feasts and serve with gladness of heart.
- Solomon gave the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asked. People assume this was sexual, but her desire was to know his wisdom and see his order; the word desire in scripture does not always mean what people think, as the law shows the tithe money could be spent on whatever the soul lusted after, meaning oxen, sheep, wine, and food.
- Nothing is said of her being pregnant. The Ethiopian tradition claims Solomon fathered a son with her and founded a dynasty, but the scripture gives no such thing; she turned and went to her own country with her servants.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 14:24-26](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v24)**
    > <sup>[24](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v24)</sup> And if the way be too long for thee, so that thou art not able to carry it; or if the place be too far from thee, which the Lord thy God shall choose to set his name there, when the Lord thy God hath blessed thee:
    >
    > <sup>[25](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v25)</sup> Then shalt thou turn it into money, and bind up the money in thine hand, and shalt go unto the place which the Lord thy God shall choose:
    >
    > <sup>[26](/bible/deuteronomy/14#v26)</sup> And thou shalt bestow that money for whatsoever thy soul lusteth after, for oxen, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, or for whatsoever thy soul desireth: and thou shalt eat there before the Lord thy God, and thou shalt rejoice, thou, and thine household,

    The tithe turned to money could be bestowed for whatsoever the soul lusteth after, meaning oxen, sheep, wine, and food, not sex.

**[1 Kings 10:14-22](/bible/1-kings/10#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/1-kings/10#v14)</sup> Now the weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred threescore and six talents of gold,
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-kings/10#v15)</sup> Beside that he had of the merchantmen, and of the traffick of the spice merchants, and of all the kings of Arabia, and of the governors of the country.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/1-kings/10#v16)</sup> And king Solomon made two hundred targets of beaten gold: six hundred shekels of gold went to one target.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/1-kings/10#v17)</sup> And he made three hundred shields of beaten gold; three pound of gold went to one shield: and the king put them in the house of the forest of Lebanon.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-kings/10#v18)</sup> Moreover the king made a great throne of ivory, and overlaid it with the best gold.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/1-kings/10#v19)</sup> The throne had six steps, and the top of the throne was round behind: and there were stays on either side on the place of the seat, and two lions stood beside the stays.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-kings/10#v20)</sup> And twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other upon the six steps: there was not the like made in any kingdom.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/1-kings/10#v21)</sup> And all king Solomon’s drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were of pure gold; none were of silver: it was nothing accounted of in the days of Solomon.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/1-kings/10#v22)</sup> For the king had at sea a navy of Tharshish with the navy of Hiram: once in three years came the navy of Tharshish, bringing gold, and silver, ivory, and apes, and peacocks.

- The weight of gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred sixty-six talents, besides that of the merchants and the kings of Arabia and the governors. He made two hundred targets and three hundred shields of beaten gold, and a great throne of ivory overlaid with the best gold.
- The throne had six steps, a round top, stays on either side, and two lions by the stays with twelve lions on the six steps, such as was not made in any kingdom. These standing lions were not graven images to bow down to; the law forbids images set up to worship, but these were not worshipped.
- All Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and the vessels of the house of the forest of Lebanon were pure gold; silver was nothing accounted of in his days. Once in three years the navy of Tarshish brought gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

  Precepts:
  - **[Leviticus 26:1](/bible/leviticus/26#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/26#v1)</sup> Ye shall make you no idols nor graven image, neither rear you up a standing image, neither shall ye set up any image of stone in your land, to bow down unto it: for I am the Lord your God.

    Make no idols nor graven image to bow down to, so the lions in Solomon's house were not for worship.

**[1 Kings 10:23-29](/bible/1-kings/10#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/1-kings/10#v23)</sup> So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and for wisdom.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/1-kings/10#v24)</sup> And all the earth sought to Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God had put in his heart.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/1-kings/10#v25)</sup> And they brought every man his present, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and armour, and spices, horses, and mules, a rate year by year.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/1-kings/10#v26)</sup> And Solomon gathered together chariots and horsemen: and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, whom he bestowed in the cities for chariots, and with the king at Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/1-kings/10#v27)</sup> And the king made silver to be in Jerusalem as stones, and cedars made he to be as the sycomore trees that are in the vale, for abundance.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/1-kings/10#v28)</sup> And Solomon had horses brought out of Egypt, and linen yarn: the king’s merchants received the linen yarn at a price.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/1-kings/10#v29)</sup> And a chariot came up and went out of Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and an horse for an hundred and fifty: and so for all the kings of the Hittites, and for the kings of Syria, did they bring them out by their means.

- Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth for riches and wisdom, and all the earth sought him to hear the wisdom the Most High put in his heart, bringing presents year by year. No king reigned like Solomon or was richer than him.
- He gathered a thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, placed in the cities and at Jerusalem; these were of his own people, so he provided jobs for them rather than making them slaves.
- He made silver in Jerusalem as stones, and had horses and linen yarn brought out of Egypt; a chariot came up for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred and fifty. Solomon bought the best of everything, but there comes a point where riches and power can pervert the mind if a man is not grounded, and that is what begins to happen.
